description:
Create an organization connector from a Valet catalog entry. It is the step after list_catalog_connectors found the entry for the product the user named; attach_connector then lets a website's pages call it.

An entry that needs no key, or whose keys the organization already holds as secrets, is created at once. An entry that needs a key from a person is not created here. Say plainly in reason why it is needed. The answer carries a request whose url the person opens, signed in to Valet, to enter each key; the connector is created when they complete it, and its name is in the answer now. Give the person the url, then follow the request with get_request. Never ask the person to type a key into this conversation. Optional keys are not asked for; the person can add them on the dashboard's Integrations page.

An entry that authorizes in a browser, OAuth or a Composio toolkit, makes a request the same way: the person opens its url, signs in to the provider from there, and the connector is created under the name in the answer. An entry the organization already has is refused, naming list_connectors; no second connector is made. Returns the connector's name, the catalog entry it came from, the slots filled from secrets the organization already held, whether a website can hold it, and the request when a person must enter keys or sign in. Requires connecting a Valet account.

entry.description: The catalog entry's name, spelled exactly as list_catalog_connectors reports it.

org_name.description: The Valet organization to create the connector in. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

reason.description: Needed when the entry requires a key or a sign-in from a person. One plain sentence, shown to the person on the request page, saying why the value is needed, such as: The app charges cards and needs your Stripe key.

name: create_connector

connector.description: The connector's name, which attach_connector takes. While request is set the connector does not exist yet; it takes this name when the person completes the request.

entry.description: The catalog entry the connector came from, in the catalog's own spelling.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

request.description: The request a person completes in the dashboard to enter a value that must not pass through this conversation. Absent when nothing needs a person.

expires_at.description: When the request expires unanswered, as an RFC 3339 UTC time.

fields.description: Names of what the person enters, never values.

id.description: Id of the request. Pass it to get_request to follow the request.

next_step.description: What to do next: give the person the url, then follow the request with get_request.

url.description: Dashboard page to give the person. They open it signed in to Valet to complete the request. It holds no credential.

secrets.description: Names of the secret slots filled from secrets the organization already held. Names only, never values. Absent when none were filled.

site_compatible.description: True when a website can hold this connector once it is created: an HTTP MCP server. False means only agents can attach it.

title: Create a connector from the catalog
